title: Chapter 180: The World in His Eyes
html:
Is he waking up?Chen Ge had no idea how many severed arms hid beneath the bed, and more monsters might be waiting outside. Lingering in the room seemed unwise. Accepting the risk of injury, he plunged through the swarm and snatched the boy from the bed.

He pressed the blade to the boy’s neck and backed toward the wall, his gaze sweeping the room. He could not understand why the arms were preventing him from harming Men Nan.

If they care about Men Nan’s safety, why would they strap him to the bed?

The Trial Mission had spun out of control the moment he passed through the door. Chen Ge had never faced anything like this and had no idea what might happen next. He tightened his grip on the cleaver. Waking Men Nan was his only option; the boy was his sole hope of surviving.

The moment the blade touched the boy’s skin, the severed arms stopped attacking. As if obeying a command, they sprang toward the door and hammered against it. The relentless knocking set Chen Ge’s nerves on edge.

Mindful of Men Nan’s warning, he had not uttered a word since entering. Even his footsteps had been as light as possible. Now the pounding echoed down the corridor, shattering the silence he had fought so hard to preserve.

Dread tightened around Chen Ge’s heart. Before he could react, a tall elderly man appeared in the doorway of the electroconvulsive-therapy room. He stood nearly six feet tall, with a head of white hair and a doctor’s coat drenched so thoroughly in blood that it had turned entirely red. Two words flashed through Chen Ge’s mind: Red Specter.

Men Nan’s warning had probably been intended to help him avoid this creature. But now that it had appeared, caution and silence no longer mattered.

“How surprising. I didn’t think anyone but me could enter this door.” The elderly man spoke with warmth and kindness. He might have looked approachable if not for the blood-soaked coat. “You don’t belong here. Put the boy down and leave at once.”

Chen Ge did not move. The boy was his only leverage, and he would not surrender it easily. Keeping the blade against the child’s neck, he studied the old man. The longer he looked, the more frightened he became.

The man’s hands were slightly mangled, as though crushed by something heavy. Something was wrong with his kindly face as well; it looked deathly, like makeup applied to a corpse.

This man has been dead for a very long time.Chen Ge’s Mortician’s Make-up talent left him certain of that.

When Chen Ge remained silent, the old man stepped into the room without changing expression. Chen Ge pressed the blade harder in response. The boy’s eyelids fluttered as if he felt the pain; he seemed close to waking.

“Don’t hurt the boy.” The senior stopped and said something curious. “If something happens to the boy, you’ll never be able to return.”

He snapped his fingers, and every severed arm withdrew beneath the bed. Chen Ge immediately took a step away from it.

“You’re far too tense. Try to relax.” The old man’s voice carried a persuasive warmth. Like Doctor Gao, he could put people at ease and lower their defenses through ordinary conversation. Whether he relied on psychological technique or something supernatural, Chen Ge could not tell. “I am the only person here who can communicate with you, and the only one who can help.”

Chen Ge did not reply. He raised the hammer with one hand and pointed at the door.

“You want to leave?” The senior shook his head. “You can leave at any time, but the boy cannot. He has to stay inside this room.”

The electroconvulsive-therapy room had the hospital’s best soundproofing. Completely isolated, it concealed everything that happened within. Trapped there with a Red Specter, Chen Ge felt panic rising. His arm tensed, pressing the blade down another few centimeters.

The old man’s face twitched, but he recovered quickly. “I’m not threatening you. Give me a chance to explain, and then you can decide.

“You might not believe this, but we are living in this boy’s nightmare. If something happens to him, or if he wakes up, we will forever be trapped here.”

“A nightmare?” These were the first words Chen Ge had spoken since entering. He watched the old man’s reaction closely. When nothing happened to his own body, he relaxed slightly.

“Yes. The boy grew up in a mental hospital, and for many reasons, he developed a deeply distorted view of the world.” What the old man said next struck a chord with Chen Ge. “You must have seen the dolls of pillows and bedsheets wandering the halls. To the boy, they represented the patients receiving treatment here. Medication dulled them until they became lifeless dolls. They lost interest in everything and spent their days trapped in a waking dream.”

“This is all his imagination?” Chen Ge looked at the bed. “Then how do you explain the broken arms? They don’t exist in real life.”

“The arms beneath the bed are manifestations of the boy’s fear. When he was very young, a doctor frightened him deliberately. He said a hairy hand lurked beneath every child’s bed, and if the child misbehaved, it would emerge at midnight, seize their ankle, and drag them into the darkness. That story turned severed arms into symbols of terror within the boy’s nightmare,” the old man explained.

“There is also a lanky monster in this nightmare that likes to perch on people’s shoulders. Such creatures embody desire. They begin no larger than an ordinary person, but as they climb onto one host after another, they drain them dry and continue to grow. Human desire has no bottom; once it exceeds all limits, it becomes harmful and grotesque.

“There are many other examples. Everything in this world reflects the boy’s subconscious.”

Chen Ge could not tell whether the old man was lying. From where he stood, the supposed doctor seemed every bit as deranged as the patients.

“I know this is difficult to believe, but it is the truth. The human brain contains 150 billion synapses, and ninety-five percent of them remain untapped. If the brain is an iceberg, the vast portion beneath the surface is the subconscious.

“An adult brain is mature, but an infant’s is different. From ages one to three, a child’s brain is at its most active, and the subconscious begins to take shape. If the child’s understanding of the world is repeatedly challenged during that period, the subconscious may become extraordinarily active—active enough to supplement the conscious mind.”

In truth, Chen Ge understood little of the old man’s explanation. What he did understand was the feeling that the man was lying and trying to conceal something.
